idiom_name: protoc-gen-go-grpc service interface + server registration; net/rpc for gob-based services
implementation_notes: protoc-gen-go-grpc generates one interface for the server side and a client stub type, so the facade is a struct implementing methods such as GetFeature(ctx, *Point) (*Feature, error) whose signatures carry the request/response messages and a context for deadlines; grpc.NewServer plus the generated Register function wire it up, and clients call through the generated type. The standard library gives the same shape without protobuf: rpc.Register exposes exported methods with the (args, *reply) error signature over gob, with rpc.Dial/rpc.DialHTTP on the client. The classic hand-written form is still justified when the peer speaks a fixed non-Go protocol, in which case the coarse handlers are written by hand over the transport.
pitfalls: Handlers run concurrently with no affinity to a connection: shared facade state needs a mutex or immutability, and request-scoped values passed through context.Context must not be mutated from spawned goroutines.
Every call should carry a deadline; without one a slow facade method pins goroutines, connections and clients until they give up.
net/rpc's gob encoding only interoperates with Go peers and ignores unexported fields, so it is unsuitable as a public boundary.
